name: Brian Glick Half Butterfly System
description: Study half butterfly guard with Brian Glick course guidance, inside-position priorities, sweep decisions, and practical drills connecting half guard to offense.
summary: The Brian Glick Half Butterfly System is an independent BJJGraph guide to half butterfly decisions, connecting positional control, opponent reactions, and a practical route into offense.
overview:
Half butterfly combines a trapped leg with an inside lifting hook. The interesting question is not whether the hook can lift someone in isolation, but whether the upper body gives it a useful direction. A crossface or a lost inside frame can make a technically familiar sweep unavailable. This guide separates restoring structure from using that structure to attack.

The published course connects inside position and head alignment with sweeps, upper-body attacks, and leg entries. This guide emphasizes the sweep-and-recovery branch; the wider course includes advanced leg attacks. Under Pressure: Half Butterfly Mastery by Brian Glick is the optional instructional companion. The drills, stages, and assessments below are original BJJGraph study suggestions; use the course demonstrations and coaching for the detailed mechanics.
key_principles: The lifting hook needs useful upper-body connection.
Restore inside frames before attacking through a settled crossface.
Respond differently when weight comes forward and when it retreats.
Distinguish elevating the opponent from controlling the landing.
Keep a half-guard recovery available when the hook is cleared.
Study leg entries separately from the initial sweep drill.

key_components.description: Identify the arm and knee connections that preserve room for your butterfly hook to work.
Compare how the same lifting hook behaves when the opponent is close and when their hips withdraw.
key_components.purpose: Match the attack to the weight available.

key_components.description: Choose a familiar underhook or other coached control and observe whether it supports the sweep direction.
key_components.purpose: Keep the torso connected to the elevation.

key_components.description: Follow the reversal until you have balanced top position or have clearly returned to guard.
key_components.purpose: Treat the landing as part of the sweep.

implementation_sequence.description: Begin in half guard and establish the butterfly hook without letting the head and shoulders become flattened.
Pause and identify the upper-body control that supports your intended sweep direction.
Have the partner alternate advancing and withdrawing so you can explain when elevation is available.
Complete one coached sweep and remain connected until the resulting top position is stable.
Allow the partner to remove the hook and practise recovering half guard before starting again.

common_obstacles.obstacle: The hook lifts but the torso stays behind.
common_obstacles.solution: Review the upper-body attachment and direction before adding more leg effort.

common_obstacles.obstacle: The head is pinned before the sweep starts.
common_obstacles.solution: Return to frame recovery instead of rehearsing the same elevation under a settled crossface.

common_obstacles.obstacle: The top player withdraws and the bottom player falls flat.
common_obstacles.solution: Practise a sit-up or frame-recovery choice when the load leaves the hook.

common_obstacles.obstacle: The sweep finishes in an uncontrolled scramble.
common_obstacles.solution: End repetitions at a named top position and reduce speed through the landing.

training_methodology.drilling_approach: BJJGraph practice plan: Start with one butterfly hook in half guard. Let the top player alternate light forward pressure and withdrawal; identify whether to load the hook, sit up, or rebuild a frame before attempting a sweep. Keep the starting position consistent long enough to compare the same problem across repetitions. Add one defensive option at a time and record the first lost connection rather than only the final result.

flashcards.question: Why is a butterfly hook alone insufficient for the sweep?
flashcards.answer: The upper-body connection and available weight determine whether the hook can move the opponent in a useful direction.

flashcards.question: What changes when the top player withdraws their hips?
flashcards.answer: The hook may no longer carry useful weight, so sitting up or recovering frames can be preferable to forcing elevation.

flashcards.question: What should precede an attack from a flattened half butterfly?
flashcards.answer: Recover usable inside structure and head position before asking the lifting hook to solve a settled upper-body pin.

flashcards.question: When is the sweep drill complete?
flashcards.answer: Finish after reaching a balanced top position or identifying a clear return to guard, not at the instant the partner tips.

flashcards.question: What is the fallback if the butterfly hook is removed?
flashcards.answer: Rebuild a familiar half-guard structure and restore the hook when space returns rather than chasing the leg without frames.

flashcards.question: Why separate leg attacks from the first practice block?
flashcards.answer: Keeping the initial task to sweep and recovery makes it easier to assess structure before introducing different controls and finishing risks.
